redactor_yields.speaker: narrator
redactor_yields.text: The Redactor came apart the way a stack of cards does: a few at a time, and then all at once. They settled face up. On every one, under the black bar, the words were still there. Ink doesn't take a word away. It only covers it.

redactor_yields.speaker: redactor
redactor_yields.text: ...Let me. Please. It is one line. PATCH, fox, paper: left a friend in the rain. I can make it so it never happened. Nobody need ever read it again.

redactor_yields.speaker: redactor
redactor_yields.text: You would forget. That is what I am for. Everything in this book that hurt, I have kept from hurting. The flood. The window. The dog at the window.

redactor_yields.speaker: patch
redactor_yields.text: Drizzle. His name's Drizzle. And you didn't keep it from hurting. You just made it so there was nothing left to put right.

redactor_yields.speaker: patch
redactor_yields.text: Leave it in. All of it. The flood, the window, me running. If it's struck out I can't go back and fix it. I have to be able to find the page.

redactor_yields.speaker: narrator
redactor_yields.text: The pen slipped out of its long fingers and rolled away across the floor, drawing a thin line behind it that went nowhere. The bar across its face had smudged. Under it, very faint, a title: GRAN'S INDEX. Kept in her hand for fifty years, until the night of the flood, when something in the book had tried to spare her the reading of it.

redactor_yields.speaker: narrator
redactor_yields.text: The black bars began to lift off the walls like flakes of soot, and under them were the entries, all of them, the whole book listed and nothing left out. A long way up, in the gutter of the book, something heavy and wet turned over in its sleep.
